item.content:encoded: Mostly? Because if we don't know how it works, it's likely not a good idea to assume that we can just use it everywhere. For all the Foundation knows there are specific circumstances that the object in question hasn't been exposed to yet that cause disastrous consequences. But we can't know what or why, because it's anomalous and we don't understand why it works the way it does. All we know is that it does. And that isn't good enough to call "safe to use everywhere".

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Immovable force hitting unstoppable object? Personally, I suspect SCP-159 will "win" - 005 only works on things that are explicitly "locks", whereas 159 is able to prevent all manner of brute force entry.

Here's an idea to potentially get inside a 159-secured facility; try using electric fields to remotely induce a current in the thing, causing it to turn on even if it's not plugged in. Will the walls block the electric field?
